overview: Rapid AI advances enable historic research breakthroughs; photonic chips promise lower AI energy use; new tools benchmark and simplify AI development.

top.title: GPT 6.2 Astra solves a historical mystery
top.summary: OpenAI’s GPT‑6.2 Astra identified the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook in 22 minutes, demonstrating AI’s emerging capability for autonomous historical research.

top.title: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light
top.summary: German startup Q.ANT introduced photonic processors that use light for nonlinear calculations, aiming to cut AI data‑center energy costs when paired with GPUs.

top.title: Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5
top.summary: Using AWS Trainium3, Hugging Face generated a 10‑second video with LTX‑2.5 in ~22 seconds, matching the performance claimed by the model’s online API.

top.title: Prospero: Bloat-free, native AI coding harness with ImGui
top.summary: Prospero, a free ImGui‑based desktop app, lets AI agents control local development environments across OSes, offering a lightweight, headless coding harness.

top.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
top.summary: Google’s Android “Create My Widget” lets Pixel users craft AI‑generated home‑screen widgets, showcasing consumer‑level AI customization despite limited practical utility.

top.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
top.summary: Hugging Face released a llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon GPUs, enabling transparent tracking of local inference performance across models and quantizations.
